title: Symbolic World Models in Lean 4 for Reinforcement Learning
venue: Proceedings of the RLC Workshop on Programmatic Reinforcement Learning

publication.venue: Proceedings of the RLC Workshop on Programmatic Reinforcement Learning

mechanism.domainTask: Evolutionary synthesis of symbolic Lean world models for model-based reinforcement learning
mechanism.populationDetail: Multiple candidate world models are maintained for evolutionary search; no island or tree organization is described.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate elite archive is described.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Population size and survivor/replacement rule are not specified in the described method.
mechanism.generationDetail: Qwen3-4B is prompted to mutate a supplied Lean formula, returning a modification, extension, and simplification.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Fitness is scalar: planning-agent return averaged over k rollouts in the pragmatic setting, or F-score of predicted dynamics in the descriptive setting. These are separate runs/objectives.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Parents are selected by fitness-proportionate stochastic universal sampling with temperature t; count is unspecified and the mention of crossover does not establish multi-parent offspring fusion.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Formal symbolic world-model representation and synthesis in Lean 4 for model-based reinforcement learning are central contribution/application dimensions outside the current Chapters 3-7 mechanism taxonomy.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/Symbolic World Models in Lean 4 for Reinforcement Learning.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Replacement/survivor policy is not specified; the paper mentions crossover when introducing parent selection but only details LLM mutation, so do not infer multi-parent fusion. Pragmatic and descriptive fitness are alternative objectives, not a hybrid objective.
